cd3ddeaf74.q: What is the difference between an amicable divorce and being financially informed in divorce?
cd3ddeaf74.a: Amicable means staying out of court and not fighting, but does not automatically mean you are financially informed. One party may say 'I will take care of you' without providing supporting documentation or helping you understand what assets and debts are actually divided. Being financially informed requires documented knowledge of what you are receiving and what it means for your post-divorce life, even if the process remains amicable.

36c17d819d.q: How can small legal details in a divorce agreement create major financial problems years later?
36c17d819d.a: Catherine's personal example: she remained on the deed of the marital home after divorce but never forced her ex-spouse to refinance or remove her name. When he later became angry and threatened to sue her over an unrelated matter, she discovered she was still legally liable for the house and any mortgage debt, despite being financially stable at signing. Details about property transfers, business ownership, and post-divorce responsibilities must be addressed immediately, not deferred.

37d6712a50.q: What was the outcome for a spousal support case where AI advised a business owner that reducing payments would be easy to win?
37d6712a50.a: A man who owned an online wellness company asked AI whether a judge would reduce his spousal support payments based on lower business income. The chatbot said it would be easy to win, but never asked for financial documents or analyzed that his spending had not gone down. The request was filed, the other side used the same records to argue income had not dropped, the judge agreed after a year, and a forensic accountant later found incomplete accounting of spoiled products. It took two law firms and nearly two years to resolve what AI described as easy, and he likely overpaid support the entire time.

350e8755f2.q: What specific recommendations do divorce professionals suggest for using AI responsibly during a divorce?
350e8755f2.a: Use AI to learn terms and understand language, build a list of questions for your attorney and financial professionals, organize your thoughts or create a checklist of documents. Do not use it to decide your strategy, do not send anything it writes to your spouse, the other attorney or the court without your attorney reviewing it first, and do not let it tell you what your numbers mean because it has not seen your numbers. If you have used AI, disclose that to your attorney or financial professionals so they understand what you have been reading.
